root_cause.text: The bounds check in ext4's check_xattrs() function failed to reserve space for the 4-byte read performed by IS_LAST_ENTRY(), allowing the next entry pointer to fall within sizeof(u32) bytes of the buffer end and triggering an out-of-bounds memory access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the condition from `(void *)next >= end` to `(void *)next + sizeof(u32) > end` because the original check permitted `next` to land at `end - 1`, where `IS_LAST_ENTRY()` would read 4 bytes via `*(__u32 *)(entry)`, exceeding the valid region.

vuln_statements.explanation: This bounds check in check_xattrs() fails to properly reserve space for the 4-byte read performed by IS_LAST_ENTRY(). The check only verifies sizeof(*header) + sizeof(u32), but does not account for the additional sizeof(u32) bytes that IS_LAST_ENTRY() will read when checking if the next entry is valid. This allows the next entry pointer to fall within sizeof(u32) bytes of the buffer end, triggering an out-of-bounds memory access when IS_LAST_ENTRY() attempts to read past the allocated buffer boundary.
